children: 1938 ET - Japanese stocks may fall, tracking Wall Street's losses on Friday. Concerns among investors including those in Japan appear to be mounting over whether companies can generate sufficient AI-related profits to meet increasingly rising credit obligations. Nikkei futures opened 1,615 points lower at 63990 on the SGX. The dollar is at 157.83 yen versus Y157.86 around Friday's Tokyo market close. The Nikkei Stock Average closed 1.4% higher at 65324.29 on Friday. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1804 ET - Australian 10-year government bond yields have been drifting lower as traders question the artificial intelligence trade, says Jack Chambers, debt strategist at ANZ. Fed speakers have also appeared more cautious about further hikes, he adds. Still, this could be only a temporary reprieve as over time these factors will reverse, he says. ANZ expects the Reserve Bank of Australia and Fed will both hike at their next meetings and it seems pre-emptive to call time on the AI trade, Chambers adds. Aussie bond yields will likely be higher by the end of the year, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

This article was corrected at 0018 GMT to reflect that Japanese stocks may fall, tracking Wall Street's losses on Friday. The original version incorrectly said they may track Wall Street's losses overnight.
